question: How long before a package that never showed up counts as lost?
query: lost package claim policy: time threshold before undelivered shipment is considered lost, delivery exception, carrier investigation, refund or replacement eligibility
answer: A package counts as lost once 10 business days have passed since the expected delivery date with no delivery scan [1][2]. If tracking shows it as delivered but the customer never received it, the wait is shorter, though the passages disagree on how much shorter: 3 business days in the shipping document [1][4] versus 2 in the playbook [2]. I can't tell which is more recent, so I can't say which figure is right.

[1] shipping.md > Lost
### Late

A package is late when it has not arrived by the last day of its delivery window. Agents should
first check the carrier's tracking; most late packages are moving and arrive within two business
days. For an expedited or overnight order that misses its window, the difference between the
service paid for and standard shipping is refunded without the customer asking.

### Lost

A package is treated as lost when 10 business days have passed since the expected delivery date
with no delivery scan. At that point customer service files a claim with the carrier and, without
waiting for the claim to settle, ships a replacement at no charge. If the original package later
turns up, the customer is asked to refuse it or to return it with a free prepaid label. Lost
package replacements over $500 need Tomas Reyes's approval under the Three Lights rule, like any
other credit of that size.

A package that tracking shows as delivered but that the customer did not receive is handled the
same way after a 3 business day wait, during which the customer checks with neighbors and the
building office. The carrier is asked for the GPS delivery scan.

### Damaged on arrival

Damage must be reported within 5 days of delivery, with photos of the item and the packaging. For
items under $50, a replacement ships at once and the customer keeps or discards the damaged item;
no return is needed. For items of $50 or more, a replacement ships at once and a free prepaid
label is sent for the damaged item, which the warehouse needs for the carrier claim. Damage
reported after 5 days is handled under the warranty policy where a defect can be shown, and
otherwise at the shift lead's discretion.

Glass globes and chimneys are the most common damage. The warehouse packs every item with a glass
part in a double-wall carton with the glass separately wrapped; a damaged globe reported with a
photo is replaced from parts stock (G-600, G-ND2, CH-7) without a full-unit replacement.

[2] customer-service-playbook.md > Lost in transit
### Damaged on arrival

A customer who receives a damaged item has 5 days from delivery to report it, with photos of the
item and the box. Open a damage claim in the Hearth admin and attach the photos. Ship a
replacement right away. For items under $50 we do not ask for the damaged item back; tell the
customer to dispose of it or keep it. For items of $50 and over, send a prepaid label at no
charge and note on the ticket that the damaged item is expected.

If a fuel product arrives leaking, tell the customer not to open the box further, to put it
outside or in a garage, and to dispose of it through their county's household hazardous waste
collection. Do not ask them to ship fuel back. Replace it.

### Lost in transit

A package counts as lost when it has not arrived 10 business days after the expected delivery
date shown in tracking. Before that, ask the customer to check with neighbors and the carrier.
Once a package is lost, ship a replacement first and file the carrier claim afterwards; the
customer does not wait for the carrier. Note the carrier claim number on the ticket. If the
replacement is also fuel, confirm the address is not a PO box.

A package shown as delivered that the customer says did not arrive is handled the same way after
a 2-business-day wait, with one exception: for orders over $400, which require a signature, pull
the signature image from the carrier before replacing.

## Warranty claims

The standard warranty is 2 years from the purchase date and covers manufacturing defects. The
Sentinel 1000 and Sentinel 1000 Pro carry 5 years, the Heritage No. 7 carries 10 years,
rechargeable batteries and battery packs carry 1 year, and Second Light refurbished items carry
1 year. Mantles, globes, wicks, bulbs and fuel caps are consumables and are not covered. Drops,
water beyond the IP rating, unapproved fuel, modifications and commercial rental use are not
covered.

A customer starts a claim by emailing help@lanternsupply.example with the order number and
photos. Open a warranty claim in the Hearth admin; it issues a number in the form WC-xxxxxx, for
example WC-030517. The Repair Center decides within 5 business days whether to repair or replace,
and the choice is ours. For an approved claim, send the customer a prepaid label to the
Hagerstown Repair Center at no charge. A claim with no order number can be matched by email
address or by the serial number on the base of the lantern.

The warranty transfers with a gift but not with a resale. If a customer bought the item second
hand, explain this and offer a paid repair.

[5] faq.md > Can I send something back if I changed my mind?
## Returns and refunds

### Can I send something back if I changed my mind?

Yes. You have 40 days from the day your order was delivered to return any unused item in its
original packaging with all its accessories. Start a return on the online store, or call us, and
you will get an RA number to put on the box.

### Does the return period start when I order or when I receive it?

It starts on the delivery date recorded by the carrier, not the day you ordered or the day we
shipped. Since May 2026 the online store counts the 40 days from delivery automatically.
